answers.l: Linus Torvalds wrote the first version in about ten days in April 2005.
SVN, 2000. "CVS done right," as its authors put it.
Started the same month as Git, after the same BitKeeper license change.
Concurrent Versions System, 1986. Commits were per file, not per change.
Helix Core. Still big in game studios, where binary assets are huge.
TFVC: Microsoft’s centralized system in TFS and Azure DevOps.
IBM Rational. Exposed versions through a virtual filesystem.
Microsoft, 1990s. Its users called it Visual SourceUnsafe.
The kernel used it until 2005. When its free license was revoked, Git and Mercurial were born.
Revision Control System, Walter Tichy, 1982. One file at a time.
jj. A Git-compatible VCS where the working copy is itself a commit.
Meta’s source control client, built for huge monorepos.
Source Code Control System, Marc Rochkind, Bell Labs, 1972. Usually called the first VCS.
Built on a "theory of patches." Changes commute.
D. Richard Hipp’s VCS for SQLite. The repository is a SQLite database, with a wiki and bug tracker inside.
Canonical’s distributed VCS, behind Launchpad.
Patch-based like Darcs, with a sounder mathematical model.
Branch-heavy, built for games. Now Unity Version Control.
Content-addressed with SHA-1 hashes. Linus took ideas from it.
tla. An early distributed VCS with famously odd branch names.
Google’s internal monorepo system, serving one giant repository to tens of thousands of engineers.
Polytron Version Control System, 1985.
Borland’s enterprise VCS.
Stream-based, built around how teams promote code.
A DEC research system that combined versioning and builds.
Peer-to-peer VCS that synchronized over email.
Serena’s enterprise change management.
IBM’s Jazz-based successor to ClearCase.

nope.github: A host. Git is the VCS.
nope.gitlab: A host. Git is the VCS.
nope.bitbucket: A host, though it did start out Mercurial-only.
nope.dropbox: We have all done it. It does not count.
nope.email: Linux kernel maintainers might argue. Still no.
nope.finalv2: A naming convention, not a version control system.

traps.q: Name the version control system Linus Torvalds wrote in about ten days in April 2005.
Name the VCS that described itself as "CVS done right."
